title: Activated carbon-based nanocomposite derived from biomass for the remediation of trace heavy metals from aqueous solutions: batch and fixed-bed adsorption studies
content: Batch and fixed-bed column studies on arsenic(iii) and cadmium(ii) adsorption performance on an activated carbon-hierarchical zeolite Y (ACHZY) nanocomposite were conducted. XRD, FTIR, TEM, SEM/EDS, and BET characterizations were used to examine the structures of the samples. HZY with mesoporous channels was fabricated via a simple approach. AC was derived from walnut shell (WSAC) or corn leaf (CLAC) biomass. WSAC possesses a higher surface area than CLAC. For the batch system, the adsorption study revealed that the highest heavy metal removal percentage (97.5% for Cd(ii) and 92.3% As(iii)) was achieved at an ACHZY dosage of 0.1 g, pH 6, and an initial metal concentration of 100 µg L−1 for 60 min. Additionally, the breakthrough time was studied for the ACHZY nanocomposite under optimum conditions. Reduced initial metal concentrations and flow speed and increased bed height increased the breakthrough time. Modeling evaluations indicated outstanding correspondence with the Langmuir and Thomas models for both heavy metals. The sorption behavior of heavy metals was best described by the pseudo-second-order model. The ACHZY sorbent indicated brilliant recyclability, with negligible decline in efficiency over five cycles. The results exhibit that the fabricated nanocomposites demonstrate enduring performance for the removal of trace As(iii) and Cd(ii) from water.
